issues.description: Time semantics complected with text streaming via a 1-second timeout heuristic
issues.detail: _push_text_frame uses a wall-clock timer (1.0s of silence) to decide when to emit LLMFullResponseEndFrame. This complects two distinct concerns: (a) the value-of-the-response (the text the agent produced) and (b) the time-model of when that response is complete. The agent already gives you complete-ness signals: a single-part response ends when the part is consumed; a multi-part SSE stream ends when the async iterator terminates. Use those facts directly to bracket the response, instead of guessing from inter-frame latency. The final close block at the bottom of process_frame already does the right thing for the end-of-stream case; the timeout is a second, parallel mechanism doing the same job badly. Pick one. The timeout is INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY layered on top of a perfectly good signal.

issues.description: AWS client lifecycle complected with per-frame invocation
issues.detail: A new bedrock-agentcore client is constructed inside an `async with` for every single LLMContextFrame. The identity here (a long-lived AWS client) is being collapsed into the value of a single call. That is PLACE-ORIENTED reasoning hidden behind async sugar: each turn rebuilds connection pools, credential resolution, and signing state. The session and client are stable identities over the life of the processor; only the invocation payload is a value. Construct the client once at startup (or lazily on first frame) and close it on processor teardown. Right now the code is paying a real cost (latency, throttling risk) to avoid naming an identity it already has.

issues.description: SSE parsing complects framing, decoding, and transformation in one nested loop
issues.detail: The inner block in process_frame does four things at once: it decides if the response is multi-part (by sniffing contentType), splits bytes into lines, strips the SSE 'data: ' prefix, and calls the user transformer. That is four separable concerns braided into one nested for/if tree, which is why the single-part branch had to be written as a near-duplicate of the multi-part branch. Pull SSE line decoding out as a pure function `parse_event_stream(parts) -> iterable[str]` and a pure `parse_single(part) -> str`, then have one loop that consumes 'response lines' regardless of transport. The transformer then sees only values (strings), with no knowledge of AWS framing. Simpler, and the tests don't need a live client.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer has no error handling for non-JSON lines
issues.detail: json.loads(response_line) will raise on any malformed line, and process_frame doesn't catch it. In a streamed SSE response, a single bad line aborts the entire turn and (because of the timeout-based close logic) may leave _output_response_open=True with no End frame queued except by the timeout task. The value here is a stream of possibly-malformed events; treat malformed-ness as part of the value domain (return None, log, skip) rather than as a control-flow exception. Same applies to part.decode('utf-8') with errors='strict'.

issues.description: Public parameter name `agentArn` violates Python convention and the rest of the module
issues.detail: Everything else in the signature is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region, context_to_payload_transformer). `agentArn` is camelCase. This is a small thing but it is exactly the kind of incidental inconsistency that costs callers cognitive load forever. The fact that the underlying AWS API uses `agentRuntimeArn` is an implementation detail; the Python-facing identity should be `agent_arn`. Rename before this ships, because renaming a public kwarg later is a breaking change.

issues.description: Credentials read from env at __init__ time, then frozen for the life of the processor
issues.detail: os.getenv(...) is evaluated once in __init__ and stored in self._aws_params. For STS-issued temporary credentials (aws_session_token), that value has a TTL and will expire mid-session. Letting aioboto3 resolve credentials itself (don't pass keys at all when the caller didn't pass them) is both simpler and correct under credential rotation. Right now you're complecting 'configuration the caller gave us' with 'configuration we scraped from the environment'.

Dead state. The close-after-timeout logic doesn't consult it; it only sleeps and checks _output_response_open. If the intent was an idle-timer that resets on each frame, the current cancel/recreate-task pattern already does that. Either remove _last_text_frame_time, or replace the cancel/recreate pattern with a single task that loops on this timestamp. Pick one mechanism. PLACE-ORIENTED state that nobody reads is a small bug waiting for a future reader to assume it means something.

issues.description: `from .agent_core import *` re-exports the helper transformers as public API
issues.detail: The wildcard export will pull `default_context_to_payload_transformer` and `default_response_to_output_transformer` into the package namespace alongside the processor class. If those are meant to be public (so callers can wrap them), say so with __all__. If not, they're now part of the API by accident and you can't change their signatures without breaking users. Either define __all__ explicitly in agent_core.py or import the class by name in __init__.py. Don't let star-import decide your public surface.

review.summary: The core processor confuses three different concerns: the value (text chunks the agent produced), the identity (a long-lived AWS client and an ongoing response), and the time model (when is the response complete). The 1-second silence timeout is the clearest symptom: the code already knows when the response stream ends because the async iterator terminates, but it has added a parallel wall-clock heuristic that fires in addition, which is incidental complexity layered on a fact that was already available. The SSE-vs-single-part parsing is also braided together in one nested loop when it wants to be two pure functions feeding a single consumer of response lines. None of this is fatal, but the shape should be fixed before it accretes call sites: rename agentArn to agent_arn (breaking later), decide whether the default transformers are public, lift the AWS client to the processor's lifecycle, and let stream-end signal end-of-response instead of a timer. The question that should have been asked first: what is one agent invocation, as a value, and how do we know it is finished? Answer that and the timeout, the dead _last_text_frame_time field, and the two near-duplicate parsing branches all collapse.
